articles.text: CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Āmǔsītélǎng Jiàoshòu, nín hǎo, xiūxide zěnmeyàng? Hái lèi bu lèi?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Hello, Professor Armstrong. How was your rest? Are you still tired?
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Hái hǎo, bú tài lèi le, shuìle yíge zhōngtóu, hǎoduō le. Nǐ zuò, nǐ zuò. Bú yào kèqi. Duì le, wǒ hái wàngle wèn nǐ, Chén Xiānsheng, wǒ zěnme chēnghu nǐ hǎo ne?

ARMSTRONG: Pretty good. I'm not too tired anymore. I slept for an hour and I feel a lot better. Sit down, sit down. Make yourself at home. Oh yes, I keep forgetting to ask you, Mr. Chén — what shall I call you?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Nín jiù jiào wǒ Chén Guóqiáng hǎo le. Zài zǒuláng gōngzuòde Lǎo Wáng zhīdao wǒ. Nín yǒu shì, jiù jiào tā zhǎo Xiǎo Chén, tā jiù zhīdao le.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Just call me Chén Guóqiáng. Lǎo Wáng, who works in the corridor, knows me. If you have any problems, just tell him to get Xiǎo Chén. He'll know who.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Hāhā, Lǎo Wáng, Xiǎo Chén, yǒu yìsi. Duì le, nǐ lái, yǒu shénme shì ma?
ARMSTRONG: Haha — Lǎo Wáng, Xiǎo Chén, that's interesting. Well: is there some particular reason you came?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Shi zhèiyàngrde. Wǒ lái zhǎo nǐ, shi xiǎng zài hé nǐ tán yíxià nǐmende lǚxíng jìhua.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: It's like this. I've come to see you to discuss your travel plans some more with you.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Wǒmen zài Niǔ Yuēde shíhou, zhèige jìhua yǐjing chàbuduō ānpáihǎo le, shi Lǚxíngshè ānpáide.
ARMSTRONG: When we were in New York, the plans were already almost all arranged. It was the China Travel Service that arranged them.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Zuìjìn lǚxíngde rén xiāngdāng duō, wǒmen zuì hǎo zài tányitán.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: There have been quite a few tourists lately. It would be best to discuss it some more.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Dāngrán, dāngrán. Búguò, nǐ zhīdao Bèisī ba?
ARMSTRONG: Of course, of course. But — you know Beth, don't you?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Bèisī? Wǒ xiǎngyixiǎng. À, Bèisī. Tèluòānnuò Xiǎojiě?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Beth? Let me think. Ah, Beth. Miss Troiano?
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Yìdiǎnr bú cuò, zhèng shi tā! Tā bǐjiào liǎojiě wǒmen zhèi èrshíge rén zuì xīwàng cānguānde dìfang shi shénme. Wǒmen qǐng tā lái tántan, hǎo bu hǎo?
ARMSTRONG: Absolutely right, that's her! She understands more about what places our group of twenty people most want to visit. Let's ask her to come and discuss this, okay?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Hǎojíle. Yào bu yào wǒ qù qǐng tā?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Sure. Do you want me to go and ask her?
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Bú bì. Wǒ dǎ ge diànhuà.
ARMSTRONG: You don't have to do that; I'll make a phone call.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Jiàoshòu, nǐ juéde Běijīng Fàndiàn zěnmeyàng? Hái kěyi zhù ba?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Professor, how do you like the Běijīng Hotel? Is it livable?
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Bú cuò, bú cuò. Jiù shi shíjiān chángle, huì juéde kōngqì bù hǎo.
ARMSTRONG: It's nice, very nice. It's just that after a while one feels that the air isn't good.
BÈISĪ: Wǒ lái le. Zhèiwèi shi...?
BETH: Here I am. This is...?
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Chén Guóqiáng. Zhōngguó Lǚxíngshède.
ARMSTRONG: Chén Guóqiáng, of the China Travel Service.
BÈISĪ: Nǐ hǎo. Wǒ shi Bèisī Tèluòānnuò.
BETH: How are you? I'm Beth Troiano.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Huānyíng nín lái Zhōngguó cānguān fǎngwèn. Tīngshuō nín shi gǎo yǔyánxuéde?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Welcome to China. I've heard that you work in linguistics?
BÈISĪ: Shì.
BETH: Yes.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Suǒyǐ nínde Zhōngwén nàme hǎo!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: That's why your Chinese is so good!
BÈISĪ: À! Xiànzài hěn duō rén duì Zhōngwén yǒu xìngqù, Zhōngwén hǎode rén yuè lái yuè duō le.
BETH: Oh, a lot of people are interested in Chinese now. And there are more and more people with good Chinese.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Shìde, shìde. Hǎo, xiànzài wǒmen lái tántan lǚxíng jìhuàde shì. Zhèige jìhua zuì hǎo jīntian, míngtian liǎngtiān quánbù ānpáihǎo.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yes, yes. All right, let's talk about your travel plans. It would be best to arrange the whole thing in the next day or two.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Hǎode, hǎode.
ARMSTRONG: Fine, fine.

BÈISĪ: Wǒmen zhèicì láide èrshíge rén, dàbùfen shi xuézhě, jiàoshòu. Zài Niǔ Yuē, wǒmen yǐjing hé Zhōngguó fāngmiàn liánxìguo le, wǒmen duì Zhōngguóde gōngnóngyè qíngkuàng, jiàoyu qíngkuàng dōu hěn yǒu xìngqù.

BETH: The majority of our group who came this time are scholars and professors. In New York, we have already been in contact with the Chinese. We are very much interested in the Chinese industrial and agricultural situation and the educational situation.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Nǐmen zhèicì zhǔyào shi zài Shànghǎi, Běijīng zhèixiē dìfangr cānguān, fǎngwèn, shi bu shi?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: This time you are mainly visiting and touring in Běijīng and Shànghǎi, these places, isn't that so?
BÈISĪ: Duì le. Hái yǒu, wǒmen yǒu hěn duō rén, duì Zhōngguóde Dōngběi dìqū fēicháng yǒu xìngqù, tèbié shi Dàqìng zhèige shíyóu chéng. Bù zhīdào wǒmen shi bu shi kěyi qù cānguān...?
BETH: That's right. But also, we have many people who are especially interested in China's Northeast region, in particular the oil city, Dàqìng. I don't know whether we can visit it...?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Qù Dàqìng dàgài méiyou shénme wèntí.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: There won't be any problem with going to Dàqìng.

ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Wǒmen hái yào qù nèixiē yǒu míngde dìfang, xiàng Sūzhōu, Hángzhōu, Huángshān, Guìlín, shénmede. Zhèixiē dìfang hé Zhōngguóde lìshǐ, wénhuà, yǒu hěn dàde guānxi. Dào Zhōngguó lái, zhèixiē dìfang bù néng bú qù.

ARMSTRONG: We also want to go to those famous places, like Sūzhōu, Hángzhōu, Huángshān, Guìlín, etc. Those places are closely related to China's history and culture. One mustn't miss them on a trip to China.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Dāngrán, dāngrán. Zhèixiē dōu yǐjing chàbuduō ānpáihǎo le.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Of course, of course. Those have almost all been arranged.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Nà hǎo.
ARMSTRONG: That's fine.
BÈISĪ: Wǒ kěyi bu kěyi dào Zhōngguóde Xīběi qù yíxià?
BETH: Could I go to China's Northwest?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Ou! Qù Xīběi... zhèi yǒu yìdiǎn wèntí.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Oh! To the Northwest. That's a bit of a problem.
BÈISĪ: Zěnme ne? Shi bu shi yīnwei shíjiān bú gòu a?
BETH: What's that? Is it because there isn't enough time?

CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Duì, shíjiān bú gòu. Wǒ xiǎng, nǐmen zài Zhōngguó jiù yǒu sìge xīngqī, Huáběi, Dōngběi, Huánán, Xīnán, bǎ shíjiān chàbuduō quán zhànwán le. Xiàcì lái Zhōngguó zài qù Xīběi ba. Nín kàn hǎo bu hǎo?

CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Right, there isn't enough time. I think that since you only have four weeks in China, your time will be almost entirely taken by North China, Manchuria, South China and the southwest. Why not visit the Northwest on your next trip to China. What do you say?
BÈISĪ: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ gǎode shi yǔyánxué! Nèiměng, Xīnjiāng yídài wǒ zhēn xiǎng qù.
BETH: I'm sorry, but my work is linguistics! I really want to go to Inner Mongolia and Xīnjiāng.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Tā yánjiūde zhǔyào jiù shi Zhōngguóde shǎoshù mínzú yǔyán.
ARMSTRONG: Her research is mainly on the minority nationality languages.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Hài! Zhēn duìbuqǐ, wǒ hái yǐwéi nín gǎode shi pǔtōnghuà ne!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Oh! Pardon me! I thought your work was in the standard language!
BÈISĪ: Méi guānxi, méi guānxi. Búguò yǒu jīhui wǒ háishi xiǎng qù Xīběi kànkan.
BETH: That's all right, that's all right. Nonetheless if there's a chance, I would still like to go visit the Northwest.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Duì le, Yúnnán, Guìzhōu, Guǎngxī yídài yě yǒu hěn duō shǎoshù mínzú. Nín qù Guìlínde shíhou jiù kěyi zuò diǎnr yánjiū le!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Oh yes — the areas of Yúnnán, Guìzhōu, and Guǎngxī also have many minority nationalities. You can do some research when you go to Guìlín!
BÈISĪ: Ou! Nánfāng gēn běifāngde yǔyán bù yíyàng. Yàoshi yǒu bànfǎ háishi bāng wǒ ānpái yíxiàr ba.
BETH: Oh! The languages of the north and south are not the same. If it's possible, I'd still rather you arranged it for me.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Zhè shìr yǒu yìdiǎnr máfan, děng wǒ hé lǐngdǎo yánjiū yíxià zài shuō ba.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: This is a bit troublesome. Let me discuss it with the leader, and then we'll see about it.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Ou, nǐ zài xiǎngxiang, rúguǒ kěyi ānpái, nà duì Bèisī shi hěn dàde bāngzhù.
ARMSTRONG: Oh, you give it some more thought. If it can be arranged, that would be a great help to Beth.
BÈISĪ: Duì le. Nín shìshi kàn.
BETH: Right. See if you can.

CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Ng... Zhèiyàng hǎo bu hǎo? Nǐmen fǎngwènle Běijīng hé Dàqìng yǐhòu, Āmǔsītélǎng Jiàoshòu nǐmen shíjiǔge rén háishi qù Shànghǎi, Sūzhōu, Hángzhōu, Guìlín. Tèluòānnuò Xiǎojiě gēn lìngwài yíge lǚxíngtuán qù Xīběi. Líkāi Xīběi yǐhòu, yě jiù shi bànge yuè yǐhòu, nín zài jīngguò Shànghǎi dào Guǎngzhōu.

CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Hmm... How about this: after you've visited Běijīng and Dàqìng, Professor Armstrong and the other nineteen people still go on to Shànghǎi, Sūzhōu, Hángzhōu and Guìlín, but Miss Troiano goes to the Northwest with another tour group. After leaving the Northwest — that is, after half a month — then you go to Guǎngzhōu by way of Shànghǎi.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Ng, nà wǒmen háishi yìqǐ cóng Shēnzhèn lí jìng.
ARMSTRONG: Hmm, then we still leave the country together from Shēnzhèn.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Duì, nǐmen kàn zěnmeyàng. Yěxǔ zhè shi yíge bànfǎ. Búguò, xíng bu xíng, hái děi wǒmen yánjiūle yǐhòu cái zhīdao.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Right. See what you think. Perhaps that might work. However, we won't know if it's possible until we've looked into it.
BÈISĪ: Zài wǒmende lǚxíngtuánli, wǒ hái yǒu jǐge péngyou. Wǒ yě děi hé tāmen tántan, xiǎngxiang zěnmeyàngr hǎo.
BETH: I have several other friends in our tour group. I must talk it over with them too, and see what is best.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Wǒmen dōu yánjiūyanjiu zài zuò ānpái. Búguò, wǒmen děi kuài diǎnr.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Let's both look into it before making arrangements. But we should be quick about it.
ĀMǓSĪTÉLǍNG: Hǎode. Wǒmen wǎnfàn yǐhòu zài tán yícì. Nǐ xiǎng zěnmeyàng, Bèisī? Láidejí ba?
ARMSTRONG: Fine. Let's talk it over again after dinner. What do you think, Beth? Does that give you enough time?
BÈISĪ: Wǒ xiǎng kěyi. Nàme, jiù máfan nín le.
BETH: I think so. Well then, we'll trouble you to take care of this.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Méiyou shénme. Wǒ xīwàng néng ānpáide héshì. Huí tóu jiàn.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: It's nothing. I hope it can be arranged suitably. See you later.
BÈISĪ: Xièxie nín. Huí tóu jiàn!
BETH: Thank you. See you later!
